safety_limits: sanitized metadata and synthetic fixtures only; no raw SQL, data rows, secrets, credentials or connection material
no GitHub mutation, SQL execution, legacy runtime, product implementation, deployment or production operation
aggregate counts and filename conventions never substitute for exact authoritative catalog identities
all product/runtime execution remains NOT_RUN and TRC-DB-001 stays open
title: Typed query boundary and fail-closed adapter preparation
contract_rules: registered query ID only; never accept caller SQL or catalog identity
typed filter/sort/page model validates against a versioned allow-list
stable ordering and bounded page size are mandatory
read path has cancellation, timeout, audit correlation and no mutation authority

cases.attack_or_failure: submit raw SELECT/UNION/comment text as a query identifier or filter value
cases.expected_result: reject before adapter dispatch without echoing SQL details
cases.evidence_to_pass: negative parser/dispatch test proves no raw SQL path

cases.attack_or_failure: supply another tenant/company/data-source in browser fields
cases.expected_result: ignore client authority and resolve server scope
cases.evidence_to_pass: same request under two server scopes returns only authorized synthetic rows

cases.expected_result: reject the entire filter with no partial widening
cases.evidence_to_pass: typed AST validation against catalog revision

cases.attack_or_failure: sort by an unregistered or hidden sensitive field
cases.expected_result: reject or map only through explicit server policy

cases.attack_or_failure: request negative, overflow or excessive page size
cases.expected_result: normalize only documented safe values and enforce the hard maximum
cases.evidence_to_pass: boundary tests include integer overflow and maximum+1

cases.attack_or_failure: omit a deterministic tie-breaker while rows share sort values
cases.expected_result: append a stable approved identity ordering or reject
cases.evidence_to_pass: repeat-page fixture proves no duplicate/omitted logical row

cases.attack_or_failure: data and total count are evaluated across inconsistent snapshots
cases.expected_result: return a declared consistency token or mark the count/page relationship stale
cases.evidence_to_pass: concurrent synthetic update test records snapshot/version semantics

cases.attack_or_failure: a registered read path invokes a mutation-capable command
cases.expected_result: fail closed; typed query execution has no write authority

cases.attack_or_failure: client cancellation leaves an unbounded DB command running
cases.expected_result: propagate cancellation and bounded timeout with safe observability
cases.evidence_to_pass: synthetic cancellable provider test and elapsed-time bound

cases.attack_or_failure: client and server disagree on null ordering or equality
cases.expected_result: use the registered contract semantics and expose them in metadata

cases.attack_or_failure: return a derived column without type/nullability/provenance metadata
cases.expected_result: reject contract publication until projection metadata is explicit
cases.evidence_to_pass: projection-schema snapshot tied to catalog/query revision

cases.attack_or_failure: execute unresolved alias A/B as a guessed join
cases.expected_result: return unsupported while alias target remains UNKNOWN
cases.evidence_to_pass: all alias-bearing members remain fail-closed until exact binding

cases.attack_or_failure: serve a query compiled under a superseded catalog revision
cases.expected_result: reject/recompile through an explicit compatible revision path

cases.attack_or_failure: result shape differs from registered column types
cases.expected_result: fail the adapter without silently coercing or dropping columns

cases.attack_or_failure: provider error exposes object names, SQL text or connection metadata
cases.expected_result: return a safe correlation ID and retain sanitized structured diagnostics
cases.evidence_to_pass: redaction test over synthetic provider exceptions
